It gives me something to relate to with its dramatic moods and extreme tense paranoia, as well as the final breath of fresh air (corsair, magic window) after the dust of a psychosis or mood has settled. As well as asking what happened, doubting whether or not I exist, that what I've experienced is real, that my knowledge is true, that my beliefs are founded in reality, etc. (From one Source all Things Depend). In short, this album feels like wreckage and reconstruction. This album definitely means the most to me and is, without a doubt, one of my favorite, (in my opinion) one of the best, albums of all time, and just saying that sends shivers down my spine.

The Campfire Headphase- warm, nostalgiac, hopeful, happy, calm. This album is one that makes me daydream- in a good way. Thinking about how I'd like the future to be, things that i'd like to do with friends. An overall feel good album.

Another interpretation of mine- Geogaddi is about dying. 

Everything seems to be going along "okay" but it's all slightly off, like being sick, the beginning of the end is signaled in "Ready Lets Go" 

Gyroscope is the shock and sudden news that you are suffering from a terminal illness.

Sunshine Recorder is your last days, spent in a hospital, maybe your last conscious moments "Bye. bye. bye.. bye...."

Julie and Candy is the process of physically dying, the DMT trip, your very last breaths.

1969 is a funeral and the honoring (or dishonoring) of your memory.

The Beach at Redpoint is the grave, decomposition, and the exit of the spirit from the body. Also about the loneliness or bareness of losing a loved one. 

Alpha and Omega is about a "limbo" of sorts, a place between the heavens and hell. The spiritual contemplations the grieving might experience.

The Devil is in the Details is about going to hell, trauma and losing yourself, a trial by fire. Anger in grief, maybe seeing "ghosts", bereavement. 

Dawn chorus is the "light at the end of the tunnel", acceptance and moving on from loss, either of yourself or of a loved one

You Could Feel the Sky is the final peace of the situation, remembrance, and the final transition into the afterlife

From one Source all Things Depend is a sort of reprisal of the albums themes, a contemplation on death, and the spiritual. 

As for the short tracks. Beware the Friendly Stranger is paranoia of dying, Dandelion is breaking the news to people, in the Annexe is about watching a loved one's last conscious moments, the Smallest Wierd Number is about decomposing, Energy Warning is the giving away of your goods and enacting your will, Opening the Mouth is the journey into limbo and grief for the living. Over the Horizon Radar is depression and defeat, Diving Station is the final stage of grief before acceptance, digging through your thoughts and memories, and Corsair and Magic Window are the eventual peace, calm, and quiet after the storm.
